summary: Kill-switch suite (tools/kill-switch-test.mjs): Stop/Pause/Resume work with isTauri() false, and no owner reaches an ai*, viewer or task-runner module it should not

coordination.notes: Owners found exactly as the increment says: src/lib/stopAllTasks.ts and src/lib/flowStop.ts. The third source the increment allows for (grep -rn 'runaway|cancelCommand' src/lib/*.ts) yields only a severity-example comment in aiAlertBroker.ts, which owns no stop path, so the owner list is two. tools/flow-stop-test.ts already owns the fan-out contract of stopAllTaskBackends against two fakes; this suite deliberately does not restate those cases and asks the different question -- does the real wiring survive a missing backend. The Tauri double reuses the mock.module pattern established by tools/backlog-test.mjs rather than adding a second way to stub that module.

findings.category: python and node-runner imports by a kill-switch owner
findings.judgement: Real, recorded, not papered over. flowStop.ts is the wiring layer and stopping those two processes is the whole of what Stop means, so the coupling is the feature; but it does mean the kill switch cannot load with the runner modules absent, a weaker property than the safety core holds. src/lib/stopAllTasks.ts takes its backends as arguments and imports nothing at all. The suite pins the finding as an exact two-element set, so a third runner import, or any runner import reaching the core, fails rather than joining a set that quietly grows.
findings.clean: Neither owner reaches any ai* or viewer module, transitively. flowStop.ts's closure is exactly flowStop, pythonTasks, nodeTasks, stopAllTasks, tauri.

findings.what: src/lib/flowStop.ts, pythonTasks.ts and nodeTasks.ts used extensionless relative imports
findings.judgement: Fixed here (four import lines gain '.ts'), which is why those three files were added to E5's touches. Without it node cannot load any kill-switch owner, so every 'works with isTauri() false' check would have had to be a source-text check instead of running the code. gameLink.ts already writes './tauri.ts'; this makes the kill-switch owners match the convention rather than adding a bespoke loader hook to work around them.
